Google Cloud Generative AI Offering

Generative AI on Google Cloud: a layered view of models, agents, knowledge and governance built around Gemini Enterprise.

Browse all five slides

Understand the stack, then choose an entry point

This presentation organizes the Google Cloud generative AI ecosystem into layers, from infrastructure and models to knowledge, agent services, governance and user experiences. It then explores model access, agent construction and the entry points presented for employees, application builders and software teams.

Source edition: November 2026. Product names, model lists, release dates, support dates and pricing statements are reproduced from the supplied deck; this page is a presentation conversion, not an independently verified service catalog.

Generative AI on Google Cloud · Gemini Enterprise Model Garden: Gemini plus 200+ models 200+ models in Model Garden Gemini · Gemma · Imagen · Veo · Lyria · Anthropic · Meta · Mistral · Moonshot · Z.ai · Hugging Face Google's own models • Gemini 3.x: 3.1 Pro for hard reasoning, 3.5 Flash for speed • Imagen, Veo and Lyria for images, video and music • Gemma 4 open models to run anywhere Partner and open models • Anthropic Claude, including Claude Sonnet 5 (added June 2026) • Llama 4, Mistral, Kimi, GLM and other open models • One API, one bill and one governance layer Ways to deploy Pay as you go per-token pricing Provisioned reserved throughput Batch lower-cost async jobs Self-deploy open models on TPU or GPU 3

Building Agents: Runtime, Tools and Knowledge

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Generative AI on Google Cloud · Gemini Enterprise Building agents: runtime, tools and knowledge Agent Runtime Where agents run • Managed hosting, formerly Agent Engine; custom containers supported • Sessions plus Memory Bank for long-term memory • Multi-day workflows and agent-to-agent orchestration • Runs ADK, LangGraph, CrewAI or your own code ADK + Agent Studio How agents are built • ADK 2.0 (GA May 2026): open source, graph-based workflows • Agent Studio: low-code visual builder for business users • Agent Garden samples and prebuilt agents such as Deep Research • Open protocols: A2A between agents, MCP for tools Grounding + data What agents know • Grounding with Google Search for fresh, cited facts • Vertex AI Search and RAG Engine over enterprise data • BigQuery and the Agentic Data Cloud • Gemini Embedding 2 for semantic retrieval Migration note: existing Vertex AI APIs keep working, but new features ship only under Agent Platform. 4

Slide 5 of 5

Governance and Entry Points

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Generative AI on Google Cloud · Gemini Enterprise Governing it, and choosing where to start Trust and governance Agent Identity A unique cryptographic ID for every agent, mapped to authorization policies for auditing Agent Registry + Gateway Catalog approved agents, tools and skills; enforce one security policy across the fleet Model Armor + Security dashboard Screens for prompt attacks and data leaks; AI security findings in one view Simulate, evaluate, optimize Test on synthetic workloads, score agents in production, trace reasoning, refine prompts Which entry point? Gemini Enterprise app Employees, no code. Find, create, share and run agents in one secure place. Agent Platform Developers, pro-code. Any model, ADK, your own data and full governance. Google AI Studio Quick prototypes on the Gemini API; move to Agent Platform for production. Pricing: Agent Platform is pay as you go (per token, or Provisioned Throughput); the Gemini Enterprise app is a per-user subscription. 5

Frequently asked questions

What does this Google Cloud generative AI presentation cover?

The five-slide deck maps the Google Cloud generative AI stack across experiences, governance, agents, knowledge and tools, models and infrastructure.

How does the deck organize an agent application?

It separates runtime and agent services, grounding through Google Search and enterprise retrieval, model access through Model Garden, and governance through guardrails, policy, identity and observability.

Which entry points does the presentation compare?

The source deck compares the Gemini Enterprise app for employees, Agent Platform for custom development, and Google AI Studio for prototypes.

Are the model lists and product dates independently verified here?

No. This page reproduces the supplied November 2026 presentation. Model availability, product names, pricing and lifecycle dates are source-deck claims and should be checked against Google Cloud documentation before implementation.
